text:
maria: RFC follow-up on quantized attention + kernel selection. Wanted to surface a few options and get alignment before I draft the implementation PR.
kevin: thanks — main tradeoffs are accuracy vs kernel complexity. per-head scales give best quant quality for int8/4 but complicate KV layout.
sara: +1 on per-head for some LLMs we onboarded. LLaMA2 finetuned mixtures show ~0.8 ppl lift without per-head.
kevin: do we have a concrete memory tax estimate for per-head scales in the KV cache? ballpark is fine.
maria: rough calc: per-head scale (fp16) add ~2 bytes per head per token if we store as bf16? hmm, re-evaluating: if we store scales separately it's heads * seq_len * sizeof(scale). for 32 heads, seq=2048, fp16 -> ~128KB per batch item.
devon: correct, and that multiplies with batch. But we can compress scales to int8 with a global multiplier, or store per-layer multipliers + per-head residuals (tiny).
sara: question: do we want kernel selector to expose "supports_per_head_scale" boolean and a fallback ordering?
kevin: yes. I propose kernel metadata API:```
register_kernel(name, {
  precision: "int8|fp8|int4|fp16",
  per_head_scale: true|false,
  kv_layout: "interleaved|separate",
  max_seq: 4096,
  preferred_batch_range: "1-8",
})
```
maria: that looks good. runtime can pick the highest-performance kernel compatible with model meta and request shape. Need to also encode accuracy tier so we can prefer higher-accuracy kernels when customer opts-in.
devon: on fallback semantics: if no fused dequant+attn kernel exists, runtime should fall back to a staged path: (1) dequantize into fp16 buffer (memory heavy), (2) run fp16 attn. We could also do on-the-fly dequant streams but those hurt latency.
kevin: and we should support a "graceful degrade" policy per route: prefer_latency, prefer_accuracy, strict (error if unsupported).
sara: testing: I'll run perf matrix on seq len [128,512,1024,2048], batch [1,4,8], and measure latency + peak mem for fused vs fallback. can we add int4 fp8 variants?
maria: yes, include int4 and fp8. Also test mixed-precision where qkv int8 but projection fp16.
runtime-bot: benchmark job 4522 finished: fused-int8-perhead -> 1.85x latency vs fp16 at batch=1, seq=512; peak mem +12%.
devon: nice. Does job output include correctness diffs (logp, perplexity) vs fp16?
runtime-bot: job 4522 accuracy: max delta in avg logp = 0.005, top-k token diffs <0.2% over eval set.
kevin: acceptable. For API changes: we should add model-level annotation "quant_layout": {per_head_scale: true, scale_dtype: "fp16|int8"} so model provider can opt-in. runtime still validates kernel compatibility.
sara: and add unit tests that simulate partial kernel availability: ensure selector picks fallback and metrics emitted.
maria: owner: i'll write the RFC patch for kernel metadata + selector. devon: i'll prototype a minimal fused kernel shim that exposes per_head flag. kevin: i'll own the perf harness and add autotuner knobs. sara: i'll run the accuracy/perf matrix and summarize.
maria: timeline: PRs across runtime, kernels, and QA by EOD next week?
kevin: realistic: runtime + kernel shims by mid-week, perf results Thu/Fri.
sara: agreed.
maria: ok, i'll draft the RFC patch and link to this thread. thanks all. :thumbsup:
runtime-bot: CI: rfc-kernel-metadata lint passed, unit tests queued."
